INDICATION:    ? ACL tear   .

PRIOR IMAGING: None available.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanisms are intact. The patellar cartilage is intact. The trochlear cartilage is intact. The patellar soft tissues are normal.

The TT-TG interval measures 10 mm, within normal limits.

The anterior cruciate, posterior cruciate, medial collateral and lateral collateral stabilizers, including the fibular collateral collateral ligament, piriformis, biceps femoris and iliotibial tendons, appear intact. No measurable anterior tibial translation.

Medial and lateral menisci are intact. Articular cartilage of the medial and lateral femoral condyle are intact.

Small knee joint effusion. No Baker's cyst.

Bone marrow ill-defined T2 hyperintense signal within the medial patella, femoral trochlea apex and posterior medial rim.

INTERPRETATION: 
No evidence of anterior cruciate ligament injury. Medial and lateral menisci are intact. 

Bone marrow T2 signal changes of the patella and lateral femur suggestive of osseous contusion, however chondromalacia cannot be excluded. Short-term interval follow-up MRI Knee in 6 weeks could differentiate between these 2 entities. Also, clinical correlation regarding a history of direct trauma.

Findings:  There is a minor knee effusion. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL and LCL. There is mild thickening of the proximal half of MCL in keeping with a healing MCL sprain. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is mild thinning of the medial compartment articular cartilage. Conclusion: Healing proximal MCL sprain. Mild medial compartment and patellar articular cartilage degeneration.

> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> Subcutaneous edema over anterior left knee.
> The contour of ACL  appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
    Mild interstitial incresed signal intensity of PCL on T1WI  and F/S T2WI, R/O degeneration or grade 1 injury.
    Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Thickening of iliotibial band, R/O tendinosis.
> A small bone island in left distal femur.
> Thickening of iliotibial band.
Impression: 
1. C/W osteoarthritis of left knee, with grade 4 chondromalacia of patellofemoral joint.
2. Synovitis of left knee and suprapaellar bursitis and patellar plicae.
3. R/O degeneration of meniscus.
4. R/O degeneration or grade 1 injury of PCL.
5. R/O tendinosis of iliotibial band.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Sprain of right knee; 4 months of inner right knee pain after skating and running injury
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild cartilage heterogeneity along the lateral tibial plateau without focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full thickness fissuring along the medial facet and median ridge with underlying subchondral edema.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 9 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Mild patellofemoral chondrosis.
